correctness.rationale: The incompatibility graph exactly describes the stated aligned Hamming and reverse-complement constraints after filtering for exact half-GC content, unequal adjacent symbols and self-separation. Reverse complementation is a Hamming isometry and preserves eligibility. Each eligible orientation class has two members, at most one of which can be selected; reversing either representative only interchanges the two cross distances being compared. Thus the unweighted compatibility clique number of the orientation classes equals capacity. Independently, n=2 is impossible by distance alone; n=4 has 40 eligible words, four size-four quotient cliques and no size-five clique, hence 4·2^4=64 labeled maxima. At n=6 there are 344 eligible words and 7804 incompatibility edges, yielding 172 orientation classes with 1908 cross-class conflicts. A separately written integer bitset search proved no clique of size 28: each candidate-prefix greedy coloring partitions into independent sets, bounding the extension by the number of colors; the recursion branches on inclusion and removes each candidate before considering later branches, and prunes only branches that cannot beat the independently checked size-27 incumbent. The complete run visited 5,237,256 search nodes. Direct read-only witness checks establish sizes 27 at six and 136 at eight for precisely the stated constraints. Since taking subsets preserves eligibility and separation, eight is the least positive even length for 32 or 128 messages.
residual_risks: The six-symbol upper bound is an exact finite exhaustive computation, not a formal or symbolic certificate. There is no exact eight-symbol optimum asserted.

The precise adjacency condition excludes identical adjacent symbols only; it does not in general exclude tandem repeats of whole two-symbol motifs, despite the imprecise wording in the limitations. No insertions, deletions or biochemical read effects are modeled.

evidence: King's accessible abstract gives fixed-GC Hamming and reverse-complement bounds; the frozen comparison describes Aboluion et al. as constructions without this adjacency filter and Nguyen et al. as run-limited GC-constrained error coding without the same orientation condition.

Run-Length Constraint of Cyclic Reverse-Complement and Constant GC-content DNA Codes is a strong additional lead: the accessible abstract excerpt explicitly combines constant GC with a maximum number of consecutive duplicates, in a cyclic reverse-complement setting.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An exact unrestricted bound applies as an upper bound to a restricted class, but an unrestricted achievable size need not survive an adjacency restriction. A cyclic or general construction combining run limits and complement conditions would need an applicable exact upper bound and a matching lower bound for the same length, GC precision, run length, orientation and Hamming parameters. Those decisive statements were not found in the excerpts; the cyclic paper is not ruled out in full.

value.rationale: The restrictions model a finite substitution code under composition and orientation constraints. Exact exclusion of 28 codewords at length six certifies that improving the search or construction cannot deliver a five-bit payload at that block length; the eight-symbol lower bound answers the corresponding five- and seven-bit feasibility questions. This is a concrete design boundary where asymptotic results and unrestricted-distance tables do not decide the answer.
residual_risks: Value is as a finite combinatorial benchmark. It does not validate a storage channel or establish exact asymptotic or length-eight capacity.
